lines.text: 1. THE SYSTEM SHALL BE CONTROLLED BY THE BAS AND SHALL OPERATE AS FOLLOWS:
1.1 EXHAUST FANS SHALL BE ENABLED WHEN THE LIGHT SWITCH IN THE WOMEN/MEN'S RESTROOM,
SHOWER/LOCKER ROOM, OR JANITOR ROOM IS ON. EXHAUST FANS SHALL ENERGIZE WHEN OCCUPANCY
SENSOR IN THESE ROOMS IS TRIGGERED.
1.2 EXHAUST FANS SHALL DE-ENERGIZE WHEN NO OCCUPANCY IS DETECTED BY THE OCCUPANCY SENSORS FOR 15
MINUTES (ADJ.).
2. ALARMS: THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL TRANSMIT SYSTEM ALARMS TO THE GRAPHIC USER
INTERFACE (GUI). THE ONBOARD CONTROLLER SHALL, AT A MINIMUM, TRACK ALARMS LISTED IN THE I/O POINTS
LIST.
1. THE MINI-SPLIT SYSTEM SHALL REMAIN ENABLED DURING ALL HOURS.
2. MINI-SPLIT CONTROL: THE MINI-SPLIT SYSTEM SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A FACTORY FURNISHED ON-BOARD BACNET
CONTROLLER. THE MANUFACTURER SHALL USE ITS PREFERRED SEQUENCE TO MEET THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS:
A. THE SPACE AIR TEMPERATURE SETPOINT SHALL BE MONITORED
B. SYSTEM SHALL BE ENERGIZED TO MAINTAIN THE SETPOINTS 78°F (ADJ.).
3. THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL COMMUNICATE WITH THE DDC TO ALLOW THE MONITORING AND CONTROL OF I/O
POINTS LISTED HERE. THE SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED 24/7.
4. ALARMS: THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL TRANSMIT SYSTEM ALARMS TO THE GUI. THE ONBOARD CONTROLLER
SHALL, AT A MINIMUM, TRACK ALARMS LISTED IN THE I/O POINTS LIST.
A. THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE ENERGIZED AND CONTROLLED BY THE BUILDING BAS SYSTEM TO MAINTAIN A PRE-DEFINED HEATING WATER TEMPERATURE SETPOINT. ALL CONTROL
POINTS ON THE I/O POINTS LIST SHALL BE MONITORED AND/OR CONTROLLED VIA THE BAS SYSTEM THROUGH THE HMI.
B. THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED WHEN:
a. THERE IS A CALL FOR HEATING: DEFINED AS ANY HEATING WATER CONTROL VALVE OPEN MORE THAN 20% (ADJ.) FOR A PERIOD OF 5 MINS. (ADJ.).
b. OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE LESS THAN 65°F (ADJ.).
C. THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM ENABLE POINT SHALL HAVE THE CAPABILITY OF BEING COMMANDED AND/OR OVERRIDDEN FROM THE HMI BY THE USER. TO PREVENT SHORT CYCLING, THE
BOILER SYSTEM SHALL REMAIN ENABLED OR DISABLED FOR 30 MINS.(ADJ.).
D. HEATING WATER PUMPS (HWP-1 & HWP-2): THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM PUMPS SHALL BE CONTROLLED BY THE BAS SYSTEM. THE TWO HEATING WATER SYSTEM PUMPS SHALL OPERATE IN
A LEAD/STANDBY FASHION, WITH ONLY ONE PUMP RUNNING AT A TIME. THE SYSTEM PUMP SHALL RUN ANY TIME A HEATING WATER CONTROL VALVE IS OPEN MORE THAN 20% (ADJ.) FOR A
PERIOD OF 5 MINS. (ADJ.). THE MOST OPEN VALVE IN THE SYSTEM IS HENCEFORTH TERMED THE “CRITICAL CONTROL VALVE”.
a. THE LEAD PUMP SHALL RUN FIRST.
b. ON FAILURE OF THE LEAD PUMP, THE STANDBY PUMP SHALL RUN AND THE LEAD PUMP SHALL TURN OFF. CONTROL SYSTEM SHALL DISPLAY A PUMP FAILURE ALARM FOR THE LEAD PUMP
ON THE HMI.
c. THE DESIGNATED LEAD PUMP SHALL ROTATE WHEN THE PUMP RUNTIME EXCEEDS ONE WEEK (ADJ.).
d. THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM PUMP SHALL START IMMEDIATELY WHEN THE CRITICAL CONTROL VALVE SENDS A SIGNAL THAT IT IS MORE THAN 20% OPEN.
e. THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM PUMP SHALL DISABLE AFTER THE CRITICAL SYSTEM CONTROL VALVE (MOST OPEN VALVE IN THE SYSTEM) IS LESS THAN 20% OPEN.
f. FREEZE PROTECTION: THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM PUMPS SHALL RUN FOR FREEZE PROTECTION WHENEVER OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE IS LESS THAN 38°F (ADJUSTABLE). THE SYSTEM
BYPASS CONTROL VALVE SHALL MODULATE OPEN AS REQUIRED TO ALLOW BOTH SYSTEM PUMPS TO RUN (AT 40% SPEED RESPECTIVELY) AS REQUIRED FOR CIRCULATION. THE CONTROL
SYSTEM SHALL DISPLAY FREEZE ALARM ON THE HMI FOR THE TIME THIS SEQUENCE IS ON.
g. PUMP STATUS: CURRENT TRANSFORMER SHALL COMMUNICATE THE STATUS OF HEATING WATER PUMP TO THE BAS SYSTEM.
E. HEATING WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE CONTROL - RESET: THE CONTROLLER SHALL MEASURE HEATING WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE WITH A SEPARATE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SENSOR
IN THE LOOP AND MODULATE THE HEATING WATER PUMP ECM TO MAINTAIN ITS HEATING WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT. ALL SET POINTS SHALL BE DETERMINED BY TAB
CONTRACTOR AND FIELD ADJUSTED TO MEET THE REQUIREMENTS OF ACTUAL FIELD CONDITIONS. THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT SHALL BE RESET BASED ON CRITICAL HEATING
CONTROL VALVE POSITION.
a. THE ECM MINIMUM SPEED SHALL NOT DROP BELOW THE SPEED CORRESPONDING WITH 30% OF THE MAXIMUM HEATING WATER FLOW. THE TAB FIRM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR
DETERMINING THIS SPEED.
b. BAS SHALL MONITOR ALL OF THE HEATING CONTROL VALVES EVERY (5) FIVE MINUTES (ADJ.) AND USE THE MOST WIDE-OPEN VALVE POSITION IN THE ENTIRE SYSTEM AS THE CRITICAL
VALVE.
c. IF THE CRITICAL HEATING CONTROL VALVE IS MORE THAN 90% OPEN (ADJ.), THEN INCREASE THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT BY 1 PSI (ADJ.).
d. IF ALL OF THE CRITICAL HEATING CONTROL VALVES ARE LESS THAN 80% OPEN (ADJ.), THEN DECREASE THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT BY 1 PSI (ADJ.). THE MINIMUM PRESSURE
LIMIT IS THE PRESSURE CORRELATING TO THE LOWEST SPEED THE PUMP MOTOR IS ALLOWED TO BE OPERATED AT (PER GUIDELINES ABOVE).
e. THE DIFFERENTIAL SET POINT WILL BE MAINTAINED BETWEEN MAXIMUM AND MINIMUM PRESSURES. THE MAXIMUM PRESSURE LIMIT IS THE PRESSURE REQUIRED TO PROVIDE FULL
FLOW TO ALL HEATING WATER CONTROL VALVES SIMULTANEOUSLY (PER TAB).
f. IN THE EVENT THAT THE CRITICAL HEATING WATER CONTROL VALVE IS LESS THAN 80% OPEN (ADJ.), AND THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT HAS BEEN REDUCED TO THE MINIMUM
ALLOWABLE SYSTEM LIMIT, THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM BYPASS VALVE LOCATED AT THE END OF LOOP SHALL BE OPENED TO ENSURE ADEQUATE HEATING FLOW IS DELIVERED TO
PROTECT THE PUMP MOTORS.
F. HEATING WATER PUMP ALARMS:
a. FAILURE: COMMANDED ON, BUT THE STATUS IS OFF.
b. RUNNING IN HAND: COMMANDED OFF, BUT THE STATUS IS ON.
c. RUNTIME EXCEEDED: STATUS RUNTIME EXCEEDS ONE WEEK.
d. ECM FAULT
G. BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMPS: THE BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMPS SHALL BE CONSTANT SPEED AND CONTROLLED IN A LEAD/LAG FASHION. THE LEAD PUMP SHALL ROTATE WHEN ITS RUNTIME
EXCEEDS ONE WEEK (ADJ.) OR WHEN THE LEAD PUMP FAILS. WHEN THERE IS A CALL FOR HEATING THE LEAD PUMP SHALL BE ENERGIZED.
a. THE BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMP SHALL START IMMEDIATELY ON RECEIVING A BOILER START COMMAND TO PROVIDE FLOW FOR THE BOILER.
b. THE BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMP SHALL DISABLE AFTER 15 MINUTES (ADJ.) OF RECEIVING THE BOILER STOP COMMAND TO MAINTAIN FLOW UNTIL THE BOILER SHUTS DOWN.
c. BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMP ALARMS:
1. FAILURE: COMMANDED ON, BUT THE STATUS IS OFF.
2. RUNNING IN HAND: COMMANDED OFF, BUT THE STATUS IS ON.
3. RUNTIME EXCEEDED: STATUS RUNTIME EXCEEDS ONE WEEK.
d. PUMP STATUS: CURRENT TRANSFORMER SHALL COMMUNICATE THE STATUS OF BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMP TO THE BAS SYSTEM.
H. BOILER CONTROL: THE BOILER SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A BACNET COMPATIBLE STANDALONE BOILER SYSTEM CONTROLLER. THE CONTROLLER SHALL CONTROL ALL OPERATIONS AND
ENERGY INPUT (MODULATE COMBUSTION) TO MAINTAIN THE HOT WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SETPOINT. THE BOILER SYSTEM CONTROLLER SHALL BE INTERFACED TO THE BAS AND
ALLOW MONITORING AND ADJUSTMENT OF SET POINTS.
a. UNDER NORMAL CONDITIONS THE BOILER SHALL BE ENABLED WHENEVER:
1. THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM IS ENABLED.
2. AND A PROOF OF SYSTEM FLOW IS GENERATED BY A HEATING WATER SYSTEM PUMP.
b. UNDER NORMAL CONDITIONS THE BOILER SHALL START WHENEVER:
1. PROOF OF FLOW IS GENERATED BY A BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMP COMMANDED BY THE BOILER.
2. AND THE HEATING WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE IS BELOW SET POINT.
c. WHENEVER THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM IS IN FREEZE PROTECTION MODE DUE TO LOW OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE, WATER SHALL FLOW THROUGH THE BOILER CONTINUOUSLY. IF
THERE IS NO CALL FOR HEATING, BUT HEATING WATER TEMPERATURE DROPS BELOW 35°F (ADJ.), BOILER SHALL START AND INCREASE WATER TEMPERATURE TO 45°F (ADJ.)
d. THE BAS SHALL BE ABLE TO HAVE TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION WITH THE BOILER CONTROLLER AND MONITOR AND ADJUST HEATING WATER SET POINT BASED ON THE RESET STRATEGY.
e. BOILER SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE: WHEN THE BOILER START CONDITIONS ARE NOT MET, THE BOILER WILL GO THROUGH A SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE. THE BOILER WILL DISABLE FIRST AND THE
ASSOCIATED BOILER CIRCULATING PUMP SHALL DISABLE AFTER A DELAY OF 15 MINS. (ADJ.).
I. BOILER ALARMS:
a. FAILURE: COMMANDED ON, BUT THE STATUS IS OFF.
b. RUNNING IN HAND: COMMANDED OFF, BUT THE STATUS IS ON.
c. LOW FLOW: FLOW THRU THE BOILER IS BELOW SET POINT.
d. BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMP FAILURE: BOILER COMMANDS CIRCULATOR PUMP TO RUN AND NO FLOW IS GENERATED.
e. HIGH HEATING WATER SUPPLY TEMP: IF GREATER THAN 190°F (ADJUSTABLE).
f. LOW HEATING WATER SUPPLY TEMP: IF LESS THAN 120°F (ADJUSTABLE).
g. CO SENSOR: THE CO SENSOR SHALL CONTINUOUSLY MONITOR CARBON MONOXIDE CONTENT INSIDE THE MECHANICAL ROOM AND SHALL BE INTERLOCKED WITH THE BAS SYSTEM AND IF
A CO LEVEL OF MORE THAN 100 PPM IS DETECTED, IT SHALL ALARM THE BAS SYSTEM TO SHUTDOWN THE BURNER IN THE BOILER AND STOP COMBUSTION PROCESS IMMEDIATELY.
A. THE NEW AIR-COOLED CHILLER SHALL BE INSTALLED WITH A BACNET COMPATIBLE CONTROLLER THAT MODULATES REFRIGERANT FLOW FOR COOLING
BASED ON A PRE-DEFINED CHILLED WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SET POINT. THE CHILLER CONTROLLER SHALL INTERFACE WITH THE NEW BUILDING BAS
SYSTEM SO THAT THE USER CAN MONITOR AND ADJUST CHILLER CONTROL POINTS USING THE HMI. CONTRACTOR TO ENSURE CHILLER MANUFACTURER
CAN FURNISH BACNET CARD/KIT OR BACNET COMPATIBLE CONTROLLERS WITH THEIR CHILLER.
B. CHILLER WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED WHEN:
a. THERE IS A CALL FOR COOLING: DEFINED AS ANY CHILLED WATER VALVE OPEN MORE THAN 20% (ADJ.) FOR A PERIOD OF 5 MINS. (ADJ.).
b. AND OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE IS GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO 55°F (ADJ.).
C. THE CHILLER SHALL RUN WHEN THE BAS COMMANDS THE CHILLER TO START.
D. TO PREVENT SHORT CYCLING, THE CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SHALL REMAIN ENABLED OR DISABLED FOR AT LEAST 30 MINUTES (ADJ.).
E. CHILLED WATER PUMPS: THE CHILLED WATER PUMPS SHALL BE CONTROLLED BY THE BAS SYSTEM. THE LEAD PUMP SHALL RUN WHEN THE CHILLER IS
COMMANDED TO START. THE LEAD CHILLED WATER PUMP WILL ROTATE AFTER A RUNTIME OF 1 WEEK (ADJ.).
a. THE CHILLED WATER PUMP SHALL START IMMEDIATELY ON RECEIVING CHILLER START COMMAND TO PROVIDE FLOW FOR THE CHILLER.
b. THE CHILLED WATER PUMP SHALL DISABLE AFTER 15 MINUTES (ADJ.) OF RECEIVING THE CHILLER STOP COMMAND TO MAINTAIN FLOW UNTIL THE
CHILLER SHUTS DOWN.
c. CHILLED WATER PUMP ALARMS:
1. FAILURE: COMMANDED ON, BUT THE STATUS IS OFF.
2. RUNNING IN HAND: COMMANDED OFF, BUT THE STATUS IS ON.
3. RUNTIME EXCEEDED: STATUS RUNTIME EXCEEDS ONE WEEK.
4. ECM FAULT
F. CHILLER CONTROL: THE CHILLER SHALL BE INSTALLED WITH A BACNET COMPATIBLE CONTROLLER THAT SHALL MEASURE THE CHILLED WATER SUPPLY
TEMPERATURE AND MODULATE REFRIGERANT FLOW TO MAINTAIN THE CHILLED WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SET POINT. THE STANDALONE
CONTROLLER SHALL BE INTERFACED WITH THE BUILDING BAS SYSTEM AND SHALL ALLOW MONITORING AND ADJUSTMENT OF SET POINTS.
a. UNDER NORMAL CONDITIONS THE CHILLER SHALL RUN WHENEVER:
1. THE CHILLER IS CALLED TO RUN.
2. AND THERE IS A PROOF OF FLOW GENERATED BY A CHILLED WATER PUMP.
3. AND THE CHILLED WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE IS ABOVE SET POINT.
b. THE BAS SHALL BE ABLE TO HAVE TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION WITH THE CHILLER CONTROLLER AND MONITOR AND ADJUST CHILLED WATER SET
POINT BASED ON THE RESET STRATEGY.
G. CHILLED WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE CONTROL - RESET: THE CONTROLLER SHALL MEASURE CHILLED WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE WITH A
SEPARATE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SENSOR IN THE LOOP AND MODULATE THE CHILLED WATER PUMP ECM TO MAINTAIN ITS CHILLED WATER
DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT (ADJ.). THE FOLLOWING SET POINTS ARE RECOMMENDED VALUES. ALL SET POINTS SHALL BE DETERMINED BY TAB
CONTRACTOR AND FIELD ADJUSTED TO MEET THE REQUIREMENTS OF ACTUAL FIELD CONDITIONS. THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT SHALL BE
RESET BASED ON CRITICAL CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE POSITION.
a. THE ECM MINIMUM SPEED SHALL NOT DROP BELOW THE SPEED CORRESPONDING WITH 5% ABOVE THE CHILLER MANUFACTURER’S RECOMMENDED
MINIMUM CHILLED WATER FLOW (NEVER DROP BELOW THE VALUE DUE TO POSSIBLE DAMAGE TO WATER COOLED CHILLER). THE TAB FIRM WILL BE
RESPONSIBLE FOR DETERMINING THIS SPEED.
b. BAS SHALL MONITOR ALL OF THE CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVES EVERY (5) FIVE MINUTES (ADJ.) AND USE THE MOST WIDE-OPEN COIL POSITION IN
THE ENTIRE SYSTEM AS THE CRITICAL VALVE.
c. IF THE CRITICAL CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE IS MORE THAN 90% OPEN (ADJ.), THEN INCREASE THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT BY 1 PSI
(ADJ.).
d. IF ALL OF THE CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVES ARE LESS THAN 80% OPEN (ADJ.), THEN DECREASE THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT BY 1 PSI
(ADJ.). THE MINIMUM PRESSURE LIMIT IS THE PRESSURE CORRELATING TO THE LOWEST SPEED THE PUMP MOTOR IS ALLOWED TO BE OPERATED AT
(PER GUIDELINES ABOVE).
e. THE DIFFERENTIAL SET POINT WILL BE MAINTAINED BETWEEN MAXIMUM AND MINIMUM PRESSURES. THE MAXIMUM PRESSURE LIMIT IS THE
PRESSURE REQUIRED TO PROVIDE FULL FLOW TO ALL CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVES SIMULTANEOUSLY (PER TAB).
f. IN THE EVENT THAT THE CRITICAL CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE IS LESS THAN 80% OPEN (ADJ.), AND THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT HAS
BEEN REDUCED TO THE MINIMUM ALLOWABLE SYSTEM LIMIT, THE CHILLED WATER BYPASS VALVE LOCATED AT THE END OF LOOP SHALL BE OPENED
TO ENSURE ADEQUATE CHILLED FLOW IS DELIVERED TO THE CHILLER.
H. CHILLER ALARMS:
a. FAILURE: COMMANDED ON, BUT THE STATUS IS OFF.
b. RUNNING IN HAND: COMMANDED OFF, BUT THE STATUS IS ON.
c. HIGH CHILLED WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE: IF THE CHILLED WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE IS 25% (ADJ.) GREATER THAN SET POINT.
d. LOW CHILLED WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE: IF THE CHILLED WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE IS 25% (ADJ.) LESS THAN SET POINT.
e. LOW CHILLED WATER FLOW: IF THE CHILLED WATER FLOW DROPS BELOW THE CHILLER MANUFACTURER’S RECOMMENDED MINIMUM FLOW WHEN
THE CHILLER IS CALLED TO RUN.
f. NO COOLING WATER FLOW: IF THERE IS NO COOLING WATER FLOW WHEN THE CHILLER IS CALLED TO RUN.
g. FREEZE PROTECTION: IF THERE IS NO CALL FOR COOLING, OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE IS BELOW 38°F. PROVIDE ALARM AND START CHILLED WATER
PUMPS TO SEND WATER IS FLOWING THRU THE CHILLER.
h. CHILLER SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE: THE CHILLER WILL GO THROUGH A SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE IF CHILLER START CONDITIONS ARE NOT MET. THE
CHILLER WILL DISABLE FIRST AFTER GOING THROUGH ITS INTERNAL SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE AND THE LEAD CHILLED WATER PUMP SHALL DISABLE
AFTER A DELAY OF 15 MINS. (ADJ.)

heading.text: CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SEQUENCE OF OPERATION
HEATING HOT WATER SYSTEM SEQUENCE OF OPERATION

lines.text: A. THE FAN COIL UNIT WILL CONSIST OF CHILLED WATER COOLING COIL, HOT WATER HEATING COIL, INTEGRAL VARIABLE SPEED DIRECT DRIVE SUPPLY AIR FAN, RETURN AIR DAMPER, AND FILTER.
B. START/STOP CONTROL: THE FAN COIL UNIT SHALL START AND STOP BASED ON THE FOLLOWING:
a. PRESET TIME OF DAY OCCUPANCY SCHEDULE THROUGH THE BAS
b. OR UNOCCUPIED SETBACK/SET-UP CONDITIONS.
c. OR LOCAL OVERRIDE OF ZONE THERMOSTAT.
d. OR MANUAL/REMOTE OVERRIDE OF SYSTEM THROUGH THE BAS.
C. WHEN THE FAN COIL UNIT IS OFF, THE CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE SHALL BE FULLY CLOSED TO FLOW THROUGH THE COIL.

D. SUPPLY AIR FAN CONTROL: WHEN THE FAN COIL UNIT IS ENERGIZED BY OCCUPANCY SCHEDULE, THE SUPPLY AIR FAN SHALL RUN CONTINUOUSLY. THE FAN SPEED SHALL MODULATE ACCORDING TO THE MANUFACTURER'S PREFERRED SEQUENCE TO MAINTAIN A SPACE
TEMPERATURE OF 78°F (ADJ.) IN COOLING AND 68°F (ADJ.) IN HEATING.
E. SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE CONTROL:

a. COOLING: UNDER NORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS THE AVERAGING TYPE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE SENSOR (LOCATED IN UNIT DISCHARGE) WILL, ACTING THROUGH THE CONTROLLER, MODULATE THE CHILLED WATER COIL TO MAINTAIN A SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE OF 55°F
(ADJ.).

b. HEATING: UNDER NORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS THE AVERAGING TYPE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE SENSOR (LOCATED IN UNIT DISCHARGE) WILL, ACTING THROUGH THE CONTROLLER, MODULATE THE HOT WATER COIL TO MAINTAIN A SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE OF 85°F
(ADJ.).

F. UNOCCUPIED SETUP CONTROL: THE FAN COIL UNIT SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH UNOCCUPIED SETUP AND UNOCCUPIED SETBACK TEMPERATURE CONTROLS. DURING UNOCCUPIED CONDITIONS, THE BAS SHALL ENERGIZE THE CHILLED WATER COIL IF ANY ZONE’S SPACE AIR

TEMPERATURE RISES ABOVE 85°F (ADJ.) DURING UNOCCUPIED HOURS AND THE ZONE IS IN COOLING MODE. ONCE ENERGIZED, THE CHILLED WATER COIL SHALL OPERATE UNDER NORMAL CONDITIONS UNTIL SPACE TEMPERATURE DROPS TO 83°F (ADJ.) FOR UNOCCUPIED SETUP.
RETURN AIR DAMPER SHALL REMAIN FULLY OPEN TO ALLOW FLOW THROUGH THE FAN COIL UNIT.

G. FREEZE PROTECTION: AN AVERAGING TYPE MANUAL-RESET FREEZESTAT INSTALLED IN THE MIXED AIR SECTION OF THE FAN COIL UNIT SHALL FULLY OPEN THE CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE TO ALLOW FLOW THROUGH THE COIL SHOULD THE MIXED AIR TEMPERATURE DROP TO
38°F (ADJ.). THE FREEZESTAT SHALL SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS. A MANUAL RESET OF THE FREEZESTAT SHALL BE REQUIRED FOR THE FAN COIL UNIT TO RETURN TO NORMAL OPERATING CONDITION.

H. EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN: AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN SWITCH SHALL BE HARD WIRED IN TO SUPPLY FAN MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE FAN AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS WHEN THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN SWITCH IS ACTIVATED. ALL CONTROL DAMPERS
AND HYDRONIC CONTROL VALVES, REGARDLESS OF WHAT MODE THE UNIT IS IN, SHALL FULLY CLOSE WHEN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN HAS BEEN ACTIVATED.

I. THE BAS SHALL ALLOW OPERATION OF ONLY ONE COIL (EITHER HEATING OR COOLING) AT A TIME. UNDER NO CONDITION SHALL BOTH HEATING AND COOLING VALVES BE SIMULTANEOUSLY OPEN OTHER THAN WHEN THE UNIT IS IN FREEZE PROTECTION MODE.
J. ALARMS:
a. SUPPLY FAN FAILURE: A CURRENT TRANSFORMER (CT) INSTALLED ON THE SUPPLY FAN CIRCUIT SHALL SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS IF THE FAN IS COMMANDED ON AND NO CURRENT IS DETECTED.

b. FAN IN HAND: A CURRENT TRANSFORMER (CT) INSTALLED IN THE FAN MATRIX MOTOR CIRCUIT (ONE FOR EACH MOTOR IN THE MATRIX) SHALL DETECT CURRENT AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS WHEN THE FAN IS COMMANDED OFF.

c. HIGH AND LOW SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE: THE BAS SHALL MONITOR THE AVERAGING TYPE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE INSTALLED IN THE UNIT DISCHARGE AND SENDS AN ALARM IF THE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE EXCEEDS 60°F (ADJ.) OR DROPS BELOW 45°F (ADJ.).

d. HIGH SUPPLY STATIC PRESSURE ALARM: AN ADJUSTABLE TYPE HIGH STATIC PRESSURE SWITCH, INSTALLED IN THE UNIT DISCHARGE SHALL BE HARD WIRED INTO SUPPLY FAN MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE SUPPLY FAN AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS WHEN
THE SUPPLY AIR STATIC PRESSURE EXCEEDS 4” W.C. (ADJ.).

e. LOW SUPPLY STATIC PRESSURE ALARM: AN ADJUSTABLE TYPE LOW STATIC PRESSURE SWITCH, INSTALLED IN THE UNIT DISCHARGE SHALL BE HARD WIRED INTO SUPPLY FAN MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE SUPPLY FAN AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS WHEN
THE SUPPLY AIR STATIC PRESSURE DROPS BELOW 0.5” W.C. (ADJ.).

f. SMOKE DETECTOR ALARM: SMOKE DETECTOR LOCATED IN THE RETURN AIR DUCTWORK SHALL BE HARD WIRED INTO THE MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE FAN. AN AUXILIARY CONTACT WILL NOTIFY THE FIRE ALARM SYSTEM AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS.

g. CLOGGED FILTER ALARM: A DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SWITCH INSTALLED ACROSS THE FILTER SECTION WILL, THROUGH THE CONTROLLER, ACTIVATE AN ALARM WHEN THE FILTER PRESSURE LOSS EXCEEDS THE HIGH LIMIT SETPOINT OF 0.70 INCH STATIC PRESSURE (ADJ.).

h. CONDENSATE OVERFLOW ALARM: A CONDENSATE FLOAT SWITCH INSTALLED IN THE AHU CONDENSATE DRAIN SHALL BE HARD WIRED INTO THE MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE FAN. AN AUXILIARY CONTACT WILL NOTIFY AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS.

heading.text: SEQUENCE OF OPERATION VAV TERMINAL UNIT (NON-FAN POWERED):

lines.text: 1. EACH VAV TERMINAL UNIT WILL BE PROVIDED WITH A BACNET COMPATIBLE TERMINAL EQUIPMENT CONTROLLER
(TEC), A DUAL TECHNOLOGY OCCUPANCY SENSOR, A DOWNSTREAM STATIC PRESSURE SENSOR, AND A PRIMARY
MODULATING SUPPLY AIR DAMPER.
2. THE VAV SYSTEM SHALL BE CONTROLLED BY THE BAS AS FOLLOWS:
2.1 EACH VAV SHALL MONITOR ITS ASSOCIATED OCCUPANCY SENSOR IN THEIR RESPECTIVE AREA. THE GUI SHALL
DISPLAY THE STATUS OF THE OCCUPANCY SENSOR IN THE BOX'S RESPECTIVE ZONE.
2.2 SUPPLY AIR DAMPER WILL MODULATE TO BE AT AN OPEN POSITION FOR 30% OF TOTAL OUTSIDE AIR VOLUME
(CALCULATED PER ASHRAE 62.1) AT ALL TIMES.
2.3 SUPPLY AIR DAMPER WILL MODULATE 100% OPEN WHEN OCCUPANCY IS DETECTED FOR MORE THAN 5
MINUTES (ADJ.).
2.4 SUPPLY AIR WILL BE DELIVERED BASED ON DOWNSTREAM STATIC PRESSURE.
3. ALARMS:
3.1 VAV FAILURE: AN ALARM SHALL BE GENERATED WHEN THERE IS A DISCREPANCY BETWEEN DAMPER POSITION
AND OCCUPANCY.

heading.text: DEDICATED OUTSIDE AIR SYSTEM CONTROL SEQUENCE

lines.text: 1. DOAS:
1.1 THE DOAS SHALL BE A PACKAGED UNIT WITH A SUPPLY FAN AND EXHAUST FAN.
1.2 THE DOAS SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A VFD FOR THE SUPPLY FAN, AND A VFD FOR THE EXHAUST FAN.
1.3 THE DOAS SHALL BE CONTROLLED BY THE BAS AND REMAIN ENABLED AT ALL TIMES.
1.3.1 DURING UNOCCUPIED HOURS: THE DOAS SHALL RUN AT 30% OF ITS FULL LOAD AND PROVIDE A MINIMUM AMOUNT OF OA AT ALL TIMES.
1.3.2 DURING OCCUPIED HOURS: WHEN OCCUPANCY IS DETECTED FOR MORE THAN 5 MINUTES, THE DOAS SHALL RUN AT A FULL LOAD CONTINUOUSLY.
1.3.3 SUPPLY AND EXHAUST AIR VOLUME SHALL BE BASED ON THE FEEDBACK FROM AIR FLOW MEASURE STATIONS.
2. DOAS CONTROL: THE DOAS SYSTEM SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A FACTORY FURNISHED ON-BOARD BACNET CONTROLLER. THE MANUFACTURER SHALL USE ITS PREFERRED SEQUENCE TO MEET THE FOLLOWING
REQUIREMENTS:
2.1 IN COOLING, THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR THE CHILLED WATER COIL LEAVING AIR TEMPERATURE AND MODULATE CHILLED WATER FLOW TO MAINTAIN THE CHILLED WATER COIL LEAVING AIR
TEMPERATURE SET POINT OF 55°F.
2.2 IN HEATING, THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR THE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE AND MODULATE THE HOT WATER COIL TO MAINTAIN THE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE SETPOINT OF 70°F.
2.3 IN ECONOMIZER, THE UNIT SHALL RUN USING AN OUTSIDE AIR DRY-BULB BASED CONTROL STRATEGY.
3. FAN CONTROL:
3.1 SUPPLY AIR FAN: THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR DUCT STATIC PRESSURE AND MODULATE SUPPLY AIR FLOW THROUGH THE VFD TO MAINTAIN DOWNSTREAM STATIC PRESSURE SET POINT. SENSOR
LOCATION AND SETPOINT SHALL BE DETERMINED BY THE TAB FIRM.
3.2 EXHAUST AIR FAN: EXHAUST AIR SHALL MODULATE TO BE 200 CFM LESS THAN SUPPLY AIR TO MAINTAIN A POSITIVE STATIC PRESSURE FOR THE SPACE.
4. CONTROLLER:
4.1 THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL COMMUNICATE WITH THE BAS TO ALLOW AT THE MINIMUM MONITORING AND CONTROL OF I/O POINTS LISTED HERE. THE SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED BY THE
BAS. ALL CONTROL POINTS ON THE I/O POINTS LIST SHALL BE MONITORED AND CONTROLLED FROM THE GRAPHIC USER INTERFACE (GUI).
5. ALARMS:
5.1 THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL TRANSMIT SYSTEM ALARMS TO THE GUI. THE ONBOARD CONTROLLER SHALL, AT A MINIMUM, TRACK ALARMS LISTED IN THE I/O POINTS LIST.

heading.text: DEDICATED OUTSIDE AIR SYSTEM CONTROL SEQUENCE

lines.text: 1. DOAS:
1.1 THE DOAS SHALL BE A PACKAGED UNIT WITH A SUPPLY FAN AND EXHAUST FAN.
1.2 THE DOAS SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A VFD FOR THE SUPPLY FAN, AND A VFD FOR THE EXHAUST FAN.
1.3 THE DOAS SHALL BE CONTROLLED BY THE BAS AND REMAIN ENABLED AT ALL TIMES.
1.3.1 DURING OCCUPIED HOURS, THE DOAS SHALL RUN CONTINUOUSLY AND DELIVER A CONSTANT AIR VOLUME CALCULATED PER ASHRAE 62.1.
1.3.2 DURING UNOCCUPIED HOURS, THE DOAS SHALL NOT RUN UNLESS A ZONE OVERRIDE COMMAND IS RECEIVED.
1.3.3 OCCUPIED/UNOCCUPIED HOURS SHALL BE DETERMINED BY BUILDING SCHEDULE IN THE BAS.
2. DOAS CONTROL: THE DOAS SYSTEM SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A FACTORY FURNISHED ON-BOARD BACNET CONTROLLER THE MANUFACTURER SHALL USE ITS PREFERRED SEQUENCE TO MEET THE FOLLOWING
REQUIREMENTS:
2.1 IN COOLING, THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR THE CHILLED WATER COIL LEAVING AIR TEMPERATURE AND MODULATE CHILLED WATER FLOW TO MAINTAIN THE CHILLED WATER COIL LEAVING AIR
TEMPERATURE SET POINT OF 55°F.
2.2 IN HEATING, THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR THE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE AND MODULATE THE HOT WATER COIL TO MAINTAIN THE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE SETPOINT OF 70°F.
2.3 IN ECONOMIZER, THE UNIT SHALL RUN USING AN OUTSIDE AIR DRY-BULB BASED CONTROL STRATEGY.
3. FAN CONTROL:
3.1 SUPPLY AIR FAN: THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR DUCT STATIC PRESSURE AND MODULATE SUPPLY AIR FLOW THROUGH THE VFD TO MAINTAIN DOWNSTREAM STATIC PRESSURE SET POINT. SENSOR
LOCATION AND SETPOINT SHALL BE DETERMINED BY THE TAB FIRM.
3.2 EXHAUST AIR FAN: EXHAUST AIR SHALL MODULATE TO BE 200 CFM LESS THAN SUPPLY AIR TO MAINTAIN A POSITIVE STATIC PRESSURE FOR THE SPACE.
4. CONTROLLER:
4.1 THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL COMMUNICATE WITH THE BAS TO ALLOW AT THE MINIMUM MONITORING AND CONTROL OF I/O POINTS LISTED HERE. THE SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED BY THE
BAS. ALL CONTROL POINTS ON THE I/O POINTS LIST SHALL BE MONITORED AND CONTROLLED FROM THE GRAPHIC USER INTERFACE (GUI).
5. ALARMS:
5.1 THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL TRANSMIT SYSTEM ALARMS TO THE GUI. THE ONBOARD CONTROLLER SHALL, AT A MINIMUM, TRACK ALARMS LISTED IN THE I/O POINTS LIST.
